title: ASE-GUI Page Up/Down test and Mac interface
body:
* A test of Page-Up failed before (#1664). It passed or failed randomly if run a couple of times. I suspect it was a synchronization problem, so in GUI.step, I moved a check on the current movie frame inside the View.set_frame function, which now works every time.
* On Mac OS, Page-Up and Page-Down appeared as 'P' and 'P' in the menu (Previous Image, Next Image in Edit). Changing to PageUp and PageDown resolved the issue. The change should be tested by users of other operative systems and keyboards.

author: lillejanur

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: https://tkdocs.com/shipman/key-names.html <--- this page says they're called "Next" and "Prior" for example.  Should we use those names and see if that works on all platforms?
comments.label_reasoning: The comment questions whether the correct platform-agnostic key names (Next/Prior) are being used for the tkinter API, suggesting the current key names may not work correctly across all platforms.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using 'Next' and 'Prior' key names instead of the current ones for cross-platform compatibility — a concrete code change is implied.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: It is a little bit strange that the code uses "Page-Down" or "PageDown".  Is that an internal alias or something?  If so we should probably remove it and use Next and Prior.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment flags potentially incorrect or non-standard key name strings ('Page-Down'/'PageDown') being used with the tkinter API, suggesting they should be replaced with the canonical names (Next/Prior) per the API specification.

comments.author: lillejanur
comments.body:
Here is how the menu items looks for me, if I set "Next" and "Prior" for Next image and Prior. It says "N" and "P" and is not helping the user.

![Screenshot_2025-07-07_at_08.26.04](/uploads/1a8bf7730f9451e531059828763fcdef/Screenshot_2025-07-07_at_08.26.04.png)

If I use "PageUp" and "PageDown" in the menu item, this is how it looks like.

![Screenshot_2025-07-07_at_08.26.57](/uploads/93fa9576c3c610191bea8dbe2745a1da/Screenshot_2025-07-07_at_08.26.57.png)

I recall that Linux displays the string as it is written. In that case "Prior" and Next" would not be helpful for the user navigating the menu.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags the use of 'Page-Down'/'PageDown' as strange and suggests removing it in favor of 'Next' and 'Prior' — a concrete refactoring suggestion.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Is there any documentation about why these buttons would be the correct ones?  How did you figure out that this change would fix the issue?

comments.author: lillejanur
comments.body: For the internal functionality, ```<Next>``` and ```<Prior>``` are the correct names. In order for the menu item to display correctly, I found by trial and error that "PageUp" and "PageDown" worked, while "Page-Up" and "Page-Down" only displays "P". I tried now with "Prior" and "Next" when making the menu items, and it displays "P" and "N". This is most likely only a Mac issue, as I recall that menu items are just written out in plain text with Linux.

thread.actionability_reasoning: Pure questions seeking understanding about why the buttons are correct and how the fix was discovered, with no implied suggestion or requested change.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @lillejanur for the MR! While it has passed six months already, I also confirmed two issues described above have been solved with this MR. Excellent solution for the long-existing `test_movie` errors for MacOS!

Regarding the key name interpretation on MacOS, while I am also not sure, I speculate [this part in the `tk` repo](https://github.com/tcltk/tk/blob/455293d6ef2e27f1aef50eddfbe20844c3aec653/macosx/tkMacOSXMenu.c#L69) may be relevant. I imagine the name like `PageUp` is recognized by `tk`, and it assigns a specific icon.

The failures on the pipeline are not relevant to the present MR, so to make things forward, I would like to merge it now.

thread.actionability_reasoning: A meta/social comment expressing thanks, confirming the fix works, providing contextual speculation, and announcing merge intent — no code change is requested or implied.
